todays_decisions.reasoning: I agree with the Market Analyst's neutral stance: the 200-day regime filter is on, but tech, small caps and credit are soft and the note says not to add aggressively. Cash is 61% of equity, so the owner's mostly-invested goal argues for deploying, but the Skeptic and Implicator found real problems with the basket, so I approved four buys at reduced size (about $85 total) and rejected RRC. This leaves roughly $280 in cash, which is still well above target; I would rather deploy over the coming days into better-evidenced names than force it today. Lesson L1 (anchor stops to the expected fill) shaped the approvals: every approved invalidation is expressed relative to the actual fill price, and I kept the sizes small where the stop could gap or where earnings dates are unverified.

trades.thesis: Default home for idle cash with the regime filter on (SPY 6.4% above its 200-day) and breadth better than the cap-weighted index. Resized from $50: the Skeptic and Implicator are right that VTI largely duplicates VOO, so I cap the combined broad-US sleeve at about 14% of equity (VOO $60 + VTI $25) rather than 18%.
trades.invalidation: SPY closes below its 200-day average (722.77), or VTI closes more than 8% below the actual fill price.

trades.thesis: Lowest volatility on the menu (0.243), F-score 8/9, gross profitability at the 89th sector percentile, and operating cash flow above net income. It adds a first Consumer Discretionary exposure, not overlapping the staples names held. Resized from $40: the Skeptic is right that its earnings date was never verified, that cash conversion is only about 1.03x, and that the sector label may flatter it. The Implicator confirmed the diversification claim holds.
trades.invalidation: A close more than 10% below the actual fill price, or an earnings report showing operating cash flow clearly below net income.

trades.thesis: Highest gross profitability on the menu (1.27, percentile 1.0), F-score 8/9, operating cash flow about 1.9x net income, no dilution. Resized from $25 to a starter position: the Skeptic is right that it is Technology against the Market Analyst's avoid list, volatility is near the cutoff, dollar volume is thin (about $34.6M), and its earnings date is unverified. The strong fundamentals justify a small position, not a larger one.
trades.invalidation: A close more than 10% below the actual fill price (tighter than the proposed 12% given the thin liquidity), or an earnings date inside the next week that proves adverse.

Resized from $20: the Skeptic is right that the thesis is mostly diversification, volatility is 44%, and the recovery partly rides on the same Iran-deal headline as energy. rejected.why: The Skeptic's case is the strongest in the set and I agree. RRC was not ranked by the Fundamentals Analyst and has an F-score of 7 with leverage up and margin not improved. Its 10-28 earnings estimate sits inside the window and the 'already reported' argument rests only on an unread 8-K. It would be entering after a roughly 9% sector run driven by oil and Hormuz headlines. As the Implicator notes, the negative beta is not a reliable hedge, and the XLE 200-day invalidation is far too distant to protect anything. It would also be a second bet on the same Iran-deal headline as BTC. I would reconsider once the 8-K is confirmed or earnings have passed.

DPZ.thesis: High-quality, cash-backed franchisor (F-score 8/9, cfo $792M vs net income $602M, gross profitability 1.15) with a 252d beta of 0.095 (-$0.62 on this position in a 10% market drop). That makes it a genuinely defensive starter position while the tape rotates away from tech. Its top-of-sector rank is partly an artifact of the wholesale-groceries mislabel, so the case rests on its absolute quality and low beta, not on the Staples tilt. No earnings inside 5 trading days.
DPZ.invalidation: DPZ closes below $274.88 (10% under the $305.42 reference close), or a fundamentals screen (including one that reflects the Q3 results reported 10-13) drops it from the menu or shows cfo below net income.

IDXX.thesis: Quality Health Care name in a favored sector (F-score 8/9, gp_sector_pct 0.941, cfo $1,182M vs net income $1,059M, no added leverage or dilution). Sized down to $40 because its 0.814 beta (-$3.26 on this position in a 10% drop) makes it the least defensive holding in the book. Earnings are estimated for 11-02, outside the 5-day window.
IDXX.invalidation: IDXX closes below $500.22 (10% under the $555.80 reference close), or IDXX underperforms XLV by more than 5 percentage points over a 21-trading-day window.

VOO.thesis: Broad, diversified US core for idle cash while the long-term regime is on (SPY 6.1% above its 200-day, 63-day +2.69%), and the Market Analyst rates broad US equity acceptable at moderate size. This is a first lot below the $90 cap because of the mega-cap earnings week, the Iran/Hormuz tail risk and rate-hike odds; add the rest after those earnings if the regime holds.
VOO.invalidation: SPY closes below ~736.8 (within 2% of its 200-day SMA of 722.32), or HYG's 21-day return falls below -3% or HYG closes more than 3% below its 200-day.

WMT.thesis: Low-volatility defensive exposure (vol 0.263, beta about zero; not a hedge) in a favored sector (XLP +6.02% 21d), with positive sell-side sentiment and no earnings until ~11-19. Fundamentals pass the screen (F-score 7, gp_sector_pct 0.865) with no red flags. Sized below the proposal because the staples move has already run and today's upgrades may be priced in, and because it lifts the Consumer Staples label to about 22.5% of equity alongside DPZ.
WMT.invalidation: WMT closes more than 7% below entry, or XLP gives back half its 21-day gain (21-day return below ~+3%) while SPY holds, or WMT cuts guidance at its ~11-19 report.
